audit.title: Auditoría comparativa Babylon BTC Staking: hipótesis F-02
audit.hypothesis: Una delegación Bitcoin podría recibir poder de voto después de expirar si el quórum covenant se completa tras consumirse el evento EXPIRED.

source.ref_type: snapshot de main por SHA fijo; no es un tag de release

root_cause: BTCDelegation.GetStatus checks covenant quorum before applying BTC expiration, so a no-quorum delegation can remain derived PENDING after its expiry event is consumed.
Late MsgServer.AddCovenantSigs creates an ACTIVE power-distribution event without rejecting the already-expired derived status.
The finality power-distribution handler applies ACTIVE without revalidating that the delegation is currently ACTIVE; the earlier EXPIRED event has already been consumed.
hypothesis_result.known_public_finding: OpenZeppelin, State Changes at the Boundary, published 2026-04-01; same EXPIRED-to-ACTIVE event order and persistent voting-power impact.
hypothesis_result.verdict_detail: Duplicada sustancial del hallazgo de OpenZeppelin y reproducida en el SHA examinado. No hay evidencia pública suficiente para afirmar regresión frente a una corrección concreta de Babylon.

commands.failure: The safety assertion expected zero voting power but observed 2000000000 sats. The test compiled and executed.

control.cache: absent because empty protobuf distribution serializes to no bytes

late_quorum_target.scenario: EXPIRED processed without quorum; event consumed
Quorum submitted after expiry through MsgServer; ACTIVE event queued
Late ACTIVE event applied by BeginBlocker

final_run.overall_status: failure because target test correctly failed its zero-power security invariant

initial_run.interpretation: Behavioral result reproduced, but final run 38098547912 is authoritative for exact upstream base evidence.

historical_comparison.name: OpenZeppelin: State Changes at the Boundary
historical_comparison.relation: Same event ordering and persistent voting-power consequence; duplicate finding. Babylon confirmed findings according to the publication, but the exact corrective SHA/release is not identified there.

historical_comparison.name: Babylon PR #631: ignore expire events when there is no covenant quorum
historical_comparison.relation: Addresses expiry without an existing covenant quorum; does not prevent a later quorum from creating ACTIVE after EXPIRED was consumed.

historical_comparison.name: Babylon PR #1404: refactor power distribution event processing
historical_comparison.relation: Refactor and same-block ACTIVE/EXPIRED coverage; not an identified fix for the cross-block late-quorum sequence.

historical_comparison.name: Babylon v4.5.0 comparison
historical_comparison.relation: Same test SHA and same 2,000,000,000-sat reproduction. Confirms F-02 was already present in v4.5.0; does not prove whether an intervening fix was later reverted.

limitations: The test harness uses actual keeper BeginBlocker, message server, event store, and KV voting-power cache/table; the Bitcoin light-client/checkpoint inputs and finality hooks are mocked fixtures.
The integration test verifies keeper KV storage in the test application, but does not run a CometBFT node or a disk-backed IAVL commit.
Tests ran on hosted GitHub Actions Linux; no full build or mass tests were run locally on Windows.
No public commit/release explicitly tied to the OpenZeppelin F-02 correction was identified, so regression versus that fix remains unresolved.
No real Bitcoin network, testnet, mainnet, transaction, private key, credentials, or funds were used.
audit.next_step_automated: Identify the exact public commit/release Babylon associates with F-02/OpenZeppelin, then run the unchanged control and target tests against that commit, its parent, and the first release after it to distinguish an incomplete fix from a regression.
